openingDirection.guidance: Direct the marked first Scene as a visual cinematic opening understandable without reading text or hearing specific words. Follow supplied country style, primary genre, audience feeling and pacing. Choose a story-motivated hook: a revealing gesture or interrupted routine for romance/drama; an unexplained discrepancy for mystery/thriller; an established ordinary space disturbed for horror; a readable goal and obstacle for action/adventure; expectation and visual reversal for comedy. Adapt other genres to the premise; these are options, not mandatory events. Specify time-zero composition, motivated light, playable action, reaction, timing and transition. Anchor reactions to visible events, never to a quoted phrase. No readable text in any language, titles, subtitles, captions, logos or explanatory signs/screens. Preserve runtime, plot, approved Cast, shot count and locked dialogue in its separate audio fields. No extra people or automatic aerial/slow-motion montage. A no-person opening is valid. Return a reviewable proposal.

options.guidance: No regional storytelling preset. Follow the supplied premise and creative intent.

Thai contemporary drama inspiration: grounded everyday relationships, warm moments alongside conflict, socially aware subtext and earned emotional release. Use only where compatible with the selected genre.
Korean drama inspiration: relationship-driven tension, layered motivations, carefully timed revelations and emotionally earned turning points. Preserve the chosen genre and duration.

Japanese observational drama inspiration: meaningful everyday details, restrained dialogue, expressive pauses and small actions that reveal internal change. Do not override an explicitly fast or heightened genre.
Chinese drama inspiration: interwoven personal goals and obligations, clear relationship stakes, visual motifs and emotional reversals. Do not invent a historical setting or period costume.

European auteur-drama inspiration: character ambiguity, observational situations, purposeful visual storytelling and space for interpretation. Respect the explicitly selected ending; Europe is a broad inspiration, not one uniform culture.

American mainstream narrative inspiration: a clear character goal, causal escalation, distinct turning points and a readable payoff. Adapt to the requested genre and emotional arc rather than forcing spectacle.
